name: zoekt-structured-search-termination-reports
instr:
Let search callers reliably distinguish complete exhaustion from limits, deadlines, cancellation, and failures through one structured termination account. Collected, streamed, JSON, HTML, and gRPC searches must expose the same outcome without changing established matches, statistics, errors, request handling, or unrelated serialization behavior.

Every SearchResult from Searcher.Search carries one valid termination classification derived from the actual shard outcomes, repository evaluation, scheduler state, readiness, and request context. Termination merging is deterministic regardless of completion order, preserves the strongest incomplete cause, and accumulates affected-shard and match counts. Repository query adaptation preserves delegated outcomes, while pre-evaluation failure contributes failure and supplies no delegated result data. StreamSearch emits at most one terminal report, after every ordinary chunk, and never emits later chunks; sampling cannot discard that report. Protobuf conversion preserves classification, counts, cancellation ownership, and stable diagnostics, while malformed data returns an error. Returned file data remains valid and unchanged after shard references are released. JSON, HTML, unary gRPC, and streaming gRPC preserve established compatibility while presenting termination equivalent to the in-process aggregate.

A limited shard combined with an exhausted shard reports limitation deterministically and includes both contributions. Repository pr
